assumptions: Field labels (holder offsets, record stride, string offsets) describe observed pointer arithmetic only, not confirmed source-level types.
Sized-delete sizes are the second argument observed at each PLT call site.
The string fields are described as pointer/capacity pairs because each frees (pointer, capacity + 1) unless the pointer equals the record base plus the capacity offset; no wider type claim is made.
The loop-end value is loaded once at entry, so a range that changes during disposal is not modelled; the records are treated as fixed for the loop.
behavior: Record-loop teardown over a vector of 0x1d8-byte records: loop from holder+0x00 to the end loaded once from holder+0x08, disposing eleven string fields per record in the order 0x1b0, 0x190, 0x170, 0x150, 0x130, 0xd0, 0xb0, 0x80, 0x60, 0x20, 0x00 (each with the short-form rule, sized delete of capacity + 1 otherwise), then a buffer exit that returns plainly when the reloaded begin is null and otherwise tail-jumps to the sized-delete PLT freeing (begin, [holder+0x10] - begin). Writes nothing to the holder or records, never frees the holder itself, performs no canary check.

buffer_exit.free_condition: null begin returns plainly, otherwise tail-jump sized delete

consumers.note: Reached only by code, never by data. See callers.tsv for the site list.

fields.note: cursor advanced by 0x1d8 before this field's delete call
